for_the_reviewer:
Press first on the arm (d) leak gate. It is the one change of mine that can stop a real run for a reason that is not a real leak. I ran it on a full, realistic parts pass of Steps 1 to 4 (frozen question, three tagged jobs, four numbered parts, a change list) and got zero flags, and on the same text with three cross-step lines and got exactly three; but the innocent case is mine, written with the gate in view, so it shows the gate runs and not that it is right. The rule most likely to fire wrongly is the last: a mark word of the eight standing in a line that also names a numbered part. 'fixed' is excluded, because Step 2 asks for it; 'unknown' and 'held' are not, and a part whose own wording is 'the mechanism is unknown' would stop the run. The first real parts pass from a real reader is where to look, and the flagged lines are in run.stopped.json for exactly that.

Second, on what arm (k) now tests. The table and the graph are gone, and so are the four sentences that name them, but six of the seven module names still stand in five lines of the procedure (the-idea-in-depth, question-bank, by-domain, reporting, testing-against-cases, word-list; only building.md goes with the table). So P4.8 is a test of the table and the map, not of every route to a module, and a zero difference reads as 'the table and the map were not what the reader was following', never as 'nothing pointed at a module'. That is in the read-me. If you want P4.8 to reach further, say so before stage C: it is a wider edit than C1 names and it should be a decision, not mine.

Third, on the certification filter's bill, which is the pull the reviewer named in its own verdict. With no stage-B list supplied, 22 of the 32 fields are certified candidates and the counts say in words that every number is provisional on stage B. Pass --certified with stage B's list and the set can shrink to nothing, in which case P4.2 and P4.3 report holds None with 'the round did not reach this prediction rather than falsifying it'. I made that the printed verdict rather than False on purpose. Check that reading is the one you want.

Fourth, the affordance table. A4 had written instrument/affordance.json by the time I finished and the counts read it; the path is printed in every counts file. Two certified cross-step fields are named there as afforded by no arms document (test_patches and turned_own_test) and are left out of P4.2 and P4.3 with the reason. A field the table does not name is read, not excluded, which is A4's own rule in that file - worth checking that A1's reading and A4's prose agree, since they were written in parallel.

Fifth, two things I found and did not fix because no fault names them. (i) exchange._match_case carries case across, so W12's 'MIT' becomes 'NEW JERSEY' in both the document and now the question - consistent between the two, and ugly; the reviewer dropped the neighbouring exchange.forms fault as unreachable this round, and this is the same family. (ii) The arm (f) gauge now runs on every DeepSeek call over the assembled messages, which includes the text of any module the tool loop served; if a withheld sentence ever appeared in a reference file the run would stop. That is the gauge doing what it says, but it is a new way for a run to stop and it is worth knowing before stage C.

Sixth, what none of this shows. Every check above is the harness explaining itself. Nothing here bears on whether any reader works, on what the service accepts, or on what the arms will show; no live call was made and no report of this round exists. The dry documents W1, W9 and W12 are A2's, which is better than the fixture, but the stand-in replies are still this rig's own, so the later calls of every arm build because they were made to.
